- When sentiment is positive (≥0.2) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to align with mean reversion bias.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5+ in 3-5 days), model often overshoots in next 5-7 days; apply downward correction of 1-3% to avoid overreaction.
- If sentiment is consistently neutral (0.00) and price is trending upward, model underestimates; increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% to capture momentum.
- Model frequently overpredicts early in 30-day horizon when sentiment is low; apply a 0.5–1.0% downward bias for first 5–7 days if sentiment < 0.1.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days of price decline after peak), model tends to hold high; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next 3–5 days.
- When sentiment spikes and price rises, model often fails to adjust for volatility; apply a 0.5–1.0% lag correction for 3–5 days after sentiment peak.
